methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed experiments with two distinct TNBC cell lines, appropriate positive and negative controls, and stated n=3 biological replicates across multiple assays (viability, flow cytometry, drug screening). Technical replicates clearly documented. Minor gaps include lack of explicit power calculation and limited discussion of confounders in stemness phenotype interpretation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical cell-based mechanistic study with clear translational intent (drug screening platform). Demonstrates physiologically relevant features (hypoxia, drug resistance at clinical concentrations). However, model is not yet validated with patient-derived tumors, and predictive capacity has not been correlated with clinical outcomes, limiting current clinical relevance.

reporting_quality.justification: RNA-sequencing data deposited in SRA (PRJNA1414100). However, raw flow cytometry, microscopy, and viability assay data availability not explicitly stated. ARRIVE standard adherence incomplete: funding sources and conflict of interest declarations minimally addressed. Methods are detailed but reproducibility details inconsistent across assays.

novelty_literature.justification: Meaningful extension of modular tissue engineering approach from transplantation to cancer modeling is novel for this application. Demonstrates superior stemness enrichment compared to existing 3D systems (spheroids, domes). However, builds directly on authors' prior work [refs 36,44] and standard molecular techniques; not first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear structure (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions). Figures effectively communicate findings, including dose-response curves and flow cytometry results. Discussion is comprehensive but somewhat verbose in places. Grammar and clarity are excellent throughout.

key_strengths: Rigorous experimental design with validated controls and multiple independent replicates
Novel adaptation of modular tissue engineering to cancer research with superior stemness enrichment vs. existing 3D systems
Demonstrates clinically relevant drug resistance at physiologic plasma concentrations
Natural emergence of hypoxia and complex phenotypes without artificial manipulation
key_concerns: Preclinical validation only; lacks patient-derived tumor data and clinical outcome correlation
Incomplete data availability beyond RNA-seq; flow cytometry and imaging raw data not shared
Limited mechanistic insight into paclitaxel-specific resistance despite detailed observation
Model currently excludes stromal and immune components acknowledged as limitations
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, well-executed preclinical study with novel methodological contribution and rigorous design. Appropriate for Tier 3 (mid-tier oncology journals) pending minor revisions to data availability statements and mechanistic discussion depth.
